---
title: "CI split search with Rcpp"
output: github_document
---

This development file documents the Rcpp-backed split-search fast path. It is
kept separate from `dev/ci_split_search.Rmd` so the original R implementation
remains available as the reference implementation.

Package files owned by this development note:

- `R/ci_split_search_cpp.R`
- `src/ci_split_search_cpp.cpp`
- `R/RcppExports.R`
- `src/RcppExports.cpp`
- `tests/testthat/test-ci_split_search_cpp.R`
- `tests/testthat/test-verification.R`

`src/ci_split_search_cpp.cpp` is a maintained source file. This flat file
documents the R wrappers; it does not contain the C++ implementation.

The exported R-facing functions mirror the existing split-search helpers and
add the `_cpp` suffix:

- `best_numeric_split_cpp()`
- `best_factor_split_cpp()`
- `best_split_for_one_variable_cpp()`
- `best_global_ci_split_cpp()`

The global helper also accepts `vars`, an optional integer vector of predictor
ids to search. When `vars` is omitted, all columns in `x` are searched.

The roxygen source for the generated wrapper should document this argument as:

```r
#' @param vars Optional integer variable ids to search. Defaults to all columns
#'   of `x`.
```

The production tree and forest builders use the C++ split search by default:
`ci_tree_control()` sets `split_engine = "cpp"`, and the recursive builder
calls `best_global_ci_split_cpp()` on that setting. Pass
`ci_tree_control(split_engine = "R")` to use the R reference search instead.
Both engines are expected to agree on the chosen partition, and both are
covered by parity tests.

The historical development notes in the earlier sections of this record
describe the period when the C++ path was an optional experiment. They are kept
for provenance only; they are not current usage instructions.

```{r, function-ci_split_search_cpp_wrappers}
#' Greedy CI split search using Rcpp engines
#'
#' @description
#' Rcpp-backed versions of the greedy concentration-index split search helpers.
#' These functions keep the same return shape as the R split helpers, but take
#' `type` instead of a prebuilt `ci_fun`. The numeric and factor helpers use
#' the R search when a selected response row has a missing SES or outcome.
#' This preserves the reference cutpoints, child weights and row assignments.
#' Infinite SES or outcome values in the selected rows raise an error.
#'
#' @param x A numeric predictor vector.
#' @param x_full A factor predictor containing all original levels.
#' @param keep A logical vector selecting the observations currently available
#'   for splitting.
#' @param y,y_full A two-column numeric response matrix.
#' @param wt,wt_full Case weights.
#' @param varid Integer identifier of the splitting variable.
#' @param ctrl A control list created by [ci_tree_control()] or compatible.
#' @param type One of `"CI"`, `"CIg"`, `"CIc"`, or `"L"`.
#' @param return Either `"split"` or `"candidate"`.
#' @param vars Optional integer variable ids to search. Defaults to all columns
#'   of `x`.
#'
#' @return A `partysplit` object, split candidate list, or `NULL`.
#'
#' @useDynLib ineqTrees, .registration = TRUE
#' @importFrom Rcpp sourceCpp
#' @name ci_split_search_cpp
NULL

#' @rdname ci_split_search_cpp
#' @export
best_numeric_split_cpp <- function(
    x,
    y,
    wt,
    varid,
    ctrl,
    type = c("CI", "CIg", "CIc", "L"),
    return = c("split", "candidate")) {
  type <- match.arg(type)
  return <- match.arg(return)
  ctrl <- .ci_tree_normalize_control(ctrl)
  wt <- .ci_validate_weights(wt, length(x), "wt")
  x <- .ci_validate_numeric_predictor(x, "x")

  stopifnot(is.matrix(y), ncol(y) == 2L, length(x) == nrow(y),
            length(wt) == nrow(y))
  .ci_validate_ci_score_inputs(y, wt)

  # Missing response rows still define predictor cutpoints and child weight.
  # The R scorer excludes them when calculating each node's impurity.
  if (anyNA(y)) {
    return(best_numeric_split(
      x = x,
      y = y,
      wt = wt,
      varid = varid,
      ctrl = ctrl,
      ci_fun = ci_factory(type),
      return = return
    ))
  }

  if (identical(type, "L")) {
    .ci_warn_negative_l_levels(y[, 1])
  }

  # The engine scores cutpoints. R turns the winner into a partykit split.
  out <- ci_best_numeric_split_cpp_engine(
    x = as.numeric(x),
    y = y,
    wt = as.numeric(wt),
    minbucket = ctrl$minbucket,
    minprob = ctrl$minprob,
    type = type
  )

  # The engine uses a non-finite gain when no cutpoint passes its checks.
  # Return NULL so the caller can skip this predictor.
  if (!is.finite(out$gain)) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  sp <- partykit::partysplit(
    varid = as.integer(varid),
    breaks = out$cutpoint,
    index = 1:2
  )

  if (identical(return, "split")) {
    return(sp)
  }

  list(
    gain = out$gain,
    varid = as.integer(varid),
    partysplit = sp,
    split = sp,
    left = as.logical(out$left),
    type = "numeric",
    cutpoint = out$cutpoint
  )
}

#' @rdname ci_split_search_cpp
#' @export
best_factor_split_cpp <- function(
    x_full,
    keep,
    y_full,
    wt_full,
    varid,
    ctrl,
    type = c("CI", "CIg", "CIc", "L"),
    return = c("split", "candidate")) {
  type <- match.arg(type)
  return <- match.arg(return)
  ctrl <- .ci_tree_normalize_control(ctrl)
  wt_full <- .ci_validate_weights(wt_full, length(x_full), "wt_full")

  if (!is.factor(x_full)) {
    x_full <- factor(x_full)
  }
  stopifnot(is.matrix(y_full), ncol(y_full) == 2L,
            length(x_full) == nrow(y_full), length(wt_full) == nrow(y_full),
            length(keep) == nrow(y_full))

  # Retain the full level map so a code still identifies the same level
  # when the split is later used for prediction.
  full_levels <- levels(x_full)
  x <- x_full[keep]
  y <- y_full[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  wt <- wt_full[keep]
  .ci_validate_ci_score_inputs(y, wt)

  # Use the R search's level ordering and weighting for incomplete responses.
  # Pass the full factor so the split still maps to its original levels.
  if (anyNA(y)) {
    return(best_factor_split(
      x_full = x_full,
      keep = keep,
      y_full = y_full,
      wt_full = wt_full,
      varid = varid,
      ctrl = ctrl,
      ci_fun = ci_factory(type),
      return = return
    ))
  }

  if (identical(type, "L")) {
    .ci_warn_negative_l_levels(y[, 1])
  }

  code <- as.integer(x)
  out <- ci_best_factor_split_cpp_engine_controlled(
    code = code,
    y = y,
    wt = as.numeric(wt),
    n_levels = length(full_levels),
    minbucket = ctrl$minbucket,
    minprob = ctrl$minprob,
    type = type,
    factor_split = ctrl$factor_split,
    max_factor_levels_partition = ctrl$max_factor_levels_partition,
    max_factor_partitions = ctrl$max_factor_partitions
  )

  if (!is.finite(out$gain)) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  left_codes <- as.integer(out$left_codes)
  present_codes <- sort(unique(code[!is.na(code)]))
  right_codes <- setdiff(present_codes, left_codes)

  # Translate the winning codes into a prediction map over the full factor.
  # Codes absent from the scoring rows have no assigned child.
  index <- rep(NA_integer_, length(full_levels))
  index[left_codes] <- 1L
  index[right_codes] <- 2L

  sp <- partykit::partysplit(
    varid = as.integer(varid),
    index = index
  )

  if (identical(return, "split")) {
    return(sp)
  }

  list(
    gain = out$gain,
    varid = as.integer(varid),
    partysplit = sp,
    split = sp,
    left = as.logical(out$left),
    type = "factor",
    factor_split = out$factor_split,
    left_levels = full_levels[left_codes],
    right_levels = full_levels[right_codes]
  )
}

#' @rdname ci_split_search_cpp
#' @export
best_split_for_one_variable_cpp <- function(
    x,
    y,
    wt,
    varid,
    ctrl,
    type = c("CI", "CIg", "CIc", "L")) {
  type <- match.arg(type)
  stopifnot(length(x) == nrow(y), length(wt) == nrow(y))
  wt <- .ci_validate_weights(wt, nrow(y), "wt")
  ctrl <- .ci_tree_normalize_control(ctrl)

  # Use the same eligible rows as the R search. Check their total weight
  # before sending a numeric threshold or factor search to the engine.
  keep <- stats::complete.cases(y) & !is.na(x) & !is.na(wt) & wt > 0
  if (sum(wt[keep], na.rm = TRUE) < ctrl$minsplit) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  candidate <- NULL

  if (is.numeric(x) || is.integer(x)) {
    candidate <- best_numeric_split_cpp(
      x = x[keep],
      y = y[keep, , drop = FALSE],
      wt = wt[keep],
      varid = varid,
      ctrl = ctrl,
      type = type,
      return = "candidate"
    )
  } else if (is.factor(x) || is.ordered(x)) {
    candidate <- best_factor_split_cpp(
      x_full = x,
      keep = keep,
      y_full = y,
      wt_full = wt,
      varid = varid,
      ctrl = ctrl,
      type = type,
      return = "candidate"
    )
  }

  if (is.null(candidate)) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Expand the engine's mask back to the node's row positions.
  left <- rep(FALSE, length(x))
  left[keep] <- candidate$left
  candidate$left <- left
  candidate
}

#' @rdname ci_split_search_cpp
#' @export
best_global_ci_split_cpp <- function(x,
                                     y,
                                     wt,
                                     ctrl,
                                     type = c("CI", "CIg", "CIc", "L"),
                                     vars = seq_along(x)) {
  type <- match.arg(type)
  stopifnot(is.matrix(y), nrow(y) == length(wt))
  wt <- .ci_validate_weights(wt, nrow(y), "wt")
  ctrl <- .ci_tree_normalize_control(ctrl)

  vars <- as.integer(vars)
  vars <- vars[vars %in% seq_along(x)]

  if (!length(vars)) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  if (!is.null(ctrl$mtry)) {
    n_select <- min(ctrl$mtry, length(vars))
    vars <- vars[sample.int(length(vars), n_select)]
  }

  parent_impurity <- ci_factory(type)(y, wt)
  best <- NULL

  # C++ finds the best cutpoint or factor partition for each predictor.
  # Compare these gains to choose one split for the current node.
  for (j in vars) {
    candidate <- best_split_for_one_variable_cpp(
      x = x[[j]],
      y = y,
      wt = wt,
      varid = j,
      ctrl = ctrl,
      type = type
    )

    # Skip predictors with no admissible split. A tie keeps the first
    # candidate encountered in the search order.
    if (!is.null(candidate) &&
        (is.null(best) || candidate$gain > best$gain)) {
      best <- candidate
    }
  }

  if (is.null(best) ||
      !is.finite(best$gain) ||
      best$gain <= ctrl$min_gain) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Use the node's parent impurity to scale the winning gain.
  best$parent_impurity <- parent_impurity
  best$relative_gain <- .ci_relative_gain(best$gain, parent_impurity)

  if (ctrl$min_relative_gain > 0 &&
      (!is.finite(best$relative_gain) ||
       best$relative_gain <= ctrl$min_relative_gain)) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  best
}
```

```{r cpp-wrapper-example, eval=FALSE}
best_global_ci_split_cpp(
  x = predictors,
  y = y,
  wt = wt,
  ctrl = ci_tree_control(),
  type = "CI"
)
```

## Design notes

The C++ engine computes the same concentration-index gain as the R path:

1. Compute the parent CI once.
2. Search all admissible candidate splits.
3. Compute child-specific weighted fractional ranks inside each candidate child.
4. Score child nodes with the direct population-style weighted covariance,
   without a child-specific finite-sample correction.
5. Return the best gain, child membership, parent impurity, and
   parent-node relative gain for `min_relative_gain` thresholding.

The C++ functions return compact engine results. The R wrappers convert those
results into the same user-facing objects as the R split search: `partysplit`
objects for `return = "split"` and candidate lists for `return = "candidate"`.

## Verification

The tests compare the C++ path against the current R implementation for:

- numeric split search,
- factor split search with unused levels,
- mixed-predictor global split search,
- tied socioeconomic rank values.

```{r tests-ci_split_search_cpp_tied_ranks}
test_that("missing SES retains the R cutpoint, gain and row assignments", {
  x <- seq_len(7L)
  y <- cbind(ses = c(6, 1, 5, NA, 7, 3, 2), outcome = c(0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1))
  wt <- rep(1, length(x))
  ctrl <- ci_tree_control(minsplit = 1, minbucket = 2, minprob = 0)

  reference <- best_numeric_split(
    x, y, wt, 1L, ctrl, ci_factory("CI"), return = "candidate"
  )
  candidate <- best_numeric_split_cpp(x, y, wt, 1L, ctrl, return = "candidate")

  expect_equal(reference$cutpoint, 2.5)
  expect_equal(candidate$cutpoint, reference$cutpoint)
  expect_equal(candidate$gain, reference$gain)
  expect_identical(candidate$left, reference$left)
})

test_that("factor search handles missing outcomes within the selected rows", {
  x <- factor(rep(letters[1:3], each = 3L), levels = letters[1:4])
  y <- cbind(ses = 1:9, outcome = c(1, NaN, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, Inf))
  wt <- rep(1, length(x))
  keep <- seq_along(x) < length(x)

  # The missing outcome is in the search sample. The infinite value is
  # outside it and should have no influence on the split or level map.
  for (strategy in c("partition", "order")) {
    ctrl <- ci_tree_control(minbucket = 1, minprob = 0, factor_split = strategy)
    reference <- best_factor_split(
      x, keep, y, wt, 1L, ctrl, ci_factory("CI"), return = "candidate"
    )
    candidate <- best_factor_split_cpp(
      x, keep, y, wt, 1L, ctrl, return = "candidate"
    )
    expect_type(reference, "list")
    expect_equal(candidate, reference)
    expect_equal(
      best_factor_split_cpp(x, keep, y, wt, 1L, ctrl),
      reference$split
    )
  }
})

test_that("direct split wrappers reject infinity in either response column", {
  x <- 1:4
  group <- factor(c("a", "a", "b", "b"))
  keep <- rep(TRUE, 4)
  wt <- rep(1, 4)
  ctrl <- ci_tree_control(minbucket = 1, minprob = 0)

  for (column in 1:2) {
    y <- cbind(ses = x, outcome = c(0, 1, 0, 1))
    y[2L, column] <- c(Inf, -Inf)[column]
    expect_error(best_numeric_split_cpp(x, y, wt, 1L, ctrl), "finite values")
    expect_error(
      best_factor_split_cpp(group, keep, y, wt, 1L, ctrl), "finite values"
    )
  }
})

test_that("zero size limits still require positive weight on both sides", {
  x <- c(1, 1, 2, 2)
  y <- cbind(ses = 1:4, outcome = c(0, 1, 0, 1))
  keep <- rep(TRUE, 4)
  ctrl <- ci_tree_control(minbucket = 0, minprob = 0)

  # The only threshold isolates two rows whose combined case weight is zero.
  for (wt in list(c(1, 1, 0, 0), c(0, 0, 1, 1))) {
    expect_null(best_numeric_split(x, y, wt, 1L, ctrl, ci_factory("CI")))
    expect_null(best_numeric_split_cpp(x, y, wt, 1L, ctrl))
    for (strategy in c("partition", "order")) {
      ctrl$factor_split <- strategy
      expect_null(best_factor_split_cpp(factor(x), keep, y, wt, 1L, ctrl))
    }
  }
})

test_that("a small positive child retains its weight beside a large child", {
  x <- c(1, 1, 2, 2)
  group <- factor(x)
  y <- cbind(ses = 1:4, outcome = c(0, 1, 0, 1))
  wt <- c(1e16, 1e16, 1, 1)
  keep <- rep(TRUE, 4)
  ctrl <- ci_tree_control(minbucket = 1, minprob = 0)

  # Subtracting the left weight from the rounded total gives zero here.
  # Both children nevertheless contain two positive-weight observations.
  reference <- best_numeric_split(
    x, y, wt, 1L, ctrl, ci_factory("CI"), return = "candidate"
  )
  candidate <- best_numeric_split_cpp(x, y, wt, 1L, ctrl, return = "candidate")
  expect_equal(reference$cutpoint, 1.5)
  expect_equal(candidate, reference)

  for (strategy in c("partition", "order")) {
    ctrl$factor_split <- strategy
    reference <- best_factor_split(
      group, keep, y, wt, 1L, ctrl, ci_factory("CI"), return = "candidate"
    )
    candidate <- best_factor_split_cpp(
      group, keep, y, wt, 1L, ctrl, return = "candidate"
    )
    expect_type(reference, "list")
    expect_equal(candidate, reference)
  }
})

# Compare R and C++ partitions, including cases where ranks are tied.
test_that("best_global_ci_split_cpp matches R scoring with tied ranks", {
  predictors <- data.frame(
    z = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8),
    group = factor(c("a", "a", "b", "b", "c", "c", "d", "d"))
  )
  y <- cbind(
    rank = c(10, 20, 20, 40, 40, 60, 60, 80),
    outcome = c(0, 0, 1, 1, 4, 4, 5, 5)
  )
  wt <- c(1, 3, 2, 1, 4, 2, 5, 1)
  ctrl <- ci_tree_control(minsplit = 1, minbucket = 1, minprob = 0)

  current <- best_global_ci_split(
    x = predictors,
    y = y,
    wt = wt,
    ctrl = ctrl,
    ci_fun = ci_factory("CIg")
  )
  cpp <- best_global_ci_split_cpp(
    x = predictors,
    y = y,
    wt = wt,
    ctrl = ctrl,
    type = "CIg"
  )

  expect_equal(cpp$gain, current$gain, tolerance = 1e-12)
  expect_equal(cpp$varid, current$varid)
  expect_equal(cpp$left, current$left)
})

test_that("best_global_ci_split_cpp respects min_relative_gain", {
  predictors <- data.frame(
    x = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7)
  )
  y <- cbind(
    rank = c(20, 10, 40, 30, 70, 50, 60),
    outcome = c(1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1)
  )
  wt <- c(1, 3, 2, 4, 1, 2, 5)
  ctrl <- ci_tree_control(
    minsplit = 1,
    minbucket = 1,
    minprob = 0,
    min_relative_gain = 0
  )

  split <- best_global_ci_split_cpp(
    x = predictors,
    y = y,
    wt = wt,
    ctrl = ctrl,
    type = "CIg"
  )

  expect_true(is.finite(split$relative_gain))
  expect_equal(split$parent_impurity, ci_factory("CIg")(y, wt))
  expect_equal(split$relative_gain, split$gain / abs(split$parent_impurity))

  ctrl$min_relative_gain <- split$relative_gain + 1e-8
  expect_null(best_global_ci_split_cpp(
    x = predictors,
    y = y,
    wt = wt,
    ctrl = ctrl,
    type = "CIg"
  ))
})

test_that("best_factor_split_cpp uses exact partition search when requested", {
  x_full <- factor(rep(letters[1:4], each = 4), levels = letters[1:4])
  keep <- rep(TRUE, 16)
  y_full <- cbind(
    rank = c(
      0.208, 0.307, 0.331, 0.199, 0.236, 0.275, 0.591, 0.253,
      0.123, 0.230, 0.598, 0.211, 0.464, 0.647, 0.961, 0.676
    ),
    outcome = c(
      2.281, 1.853, 2.333, 2.283, 1.301, 3.502, 2.120, 1.706,
      2.906, 4.838, 3.343, 3.161, 4.298, 3.896, 4.187, 0.548
    )
  )
  wt_full <- c(
    1.649, 1.998, 2.799, 2.957, 0.595, 1.945, 2.333, 1.122,
    1.252, 2.334, 2.767, 1.025, 1.395, 1.621, 2.766, 1.474
  )
  ctrl <- ci_tree_control(
    minsplit = 1,
    minbucket = 1,
    minprob = 0,
    factor_split = "partition",
    max_factor_partitions = 1e6
  )
  expected <- best_factor_split(
    x_full, keep, y_full, wt_full, 1, ctrl, ci_factory("CI"),
    return = "candidate"
  )
  cpp <- best_factor_split_cpp(
    x_full, keep, y_full, wt_full, 1, ctrl, type = "CI",
    return = "candidate"
  )

  expect_equal(cpp$factor_split, "partition")
  expect_equal(cpp$gain, expected$gain, tolerance = 1e-12)
  expect_equal(cpp$left_levels, expected$left_levels)
})

test_that("best_factor_split_cpp falls back to ordered factor search in auto mode", {
  x_full <- factor(rep(letters[1:4], each = 2), levels = letters[1:4])
  keep <- rep(TRUE, 8)
  y_full <- cbind(
    rank = seq_len(8),
    outcome = c(1, 2, 4, 3, 7, 6, 8, 5)
  )
  wt_full <- rep(1, 8)
  ctrl <- ci_tree_control(
    minsplit = 1,
    minbucket = 1,
    minprob = 0,
    factor_split = "auto",
    max_factor_partitions = 1
  )
  cpp <- best_factor_split_cpp(
    x_full, keep, y_full, wt_full, 1, ctrl, type = "CI",
    return = "candidate"
  )

  expect_equal(cpp$factor_split, "order")
})

test_that("best_global_ci_split_cpp rejects non-finite weights before C++", {
  predictors <- data.frame(x = c(1, 2, 3))
  y <- cbind(rank = c(10, 20, 30), outcome = c(1, 0, 1))
  ctrl <- ci_tree_control(minsplit = 1, minbucket = 1, minprob = 0)

  for (bad_weights in list(c(1, Inf, 1), c(1, NaN, 1), c(1, -Inf, 1))) {
    expect_error(
      best_global_ci_split_cpp(
        x = predictors,
        y = y,
        wt = bad_weights,
        ctrl = ctrl,
        type = "CI"
      ),
      "finite"
    )
  }
})

test_that("best_global_ci_split_cpp samples mtry variable ids, not positions", {
  toy_data <- data.frame(
    rank = c(10, 20, 30, 40, 50),
    outcome = c(1, 5, 10, 20, 40),
    strong = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
  )
  y <- as.matrix(toy_data[c("rank", "outcome")])
  wt <- rep(1, nrow(toy_data))

  ctrl <- ci_tree_control(minsplit = 1, minbucket = 1, minprob = 0)
  ctrl$mtry <- 1L

  # Check across seeds that mtry samples only from the requested columns.
  for (seed in 1:20) {
    set.seed(seed)
    split <- best_global_ci_split_cpp(
      x = toy_data,
      y = y,
      wt = wt,
      ctrl = ctrl,
      type = "CI",
      vars = 3L
    )

    expect_equal(split$varid, 3L)
  }
})
```

Run focused tests with:

testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-ci_split_search_cpp.R")
